purpose: Grille and front condition correction from current real front reference; original V3 coastal scene and orbit view retained.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only the truck's front grille, front bumper superficial wear, and foglamp lens haze in IMAGE 1 (the edit target). IMAGE 2 is a close real photographic reference of this exact vehicle, ONLY a parts/condition reference, never copy its setting, framing, people, plate or light. Replace IMAGE 1's incorrect fine oval honeycomb grille with the real grille geometry shown by IMAGE 2: a matte black molded chunky grille with large horizontally rectangular/angular openings with clipped corners, horizontal block tabs, thick black middle bar with central raised geometric/chamfered outline containing large raised grey letters "TOYOTA". Closely reproduce real reference grille rather than a generic honeycomb mesh or vintage grille. Adapt perspective accurately to IMAGE 1. Front bumper stays original grey, match only subtle photographed scuffs/surface wear and foglamp lens haze from IMAGE 2 without exaggeration or inventing defects. Preserve every other pixel as closely as possible: same 1672x941 wide image, camera, exact vehicle position and scale, grey paint, beach clouds ocean dune background and shadows, roof bars running left-right across truck, side rails, silver five spoke wheels, tires, body trim, headlights and their geometry, no rear spoiler. Blank front license plate stays blank. No people, no accessories, no front hitch, no additional graphics or labels. This is a tiny local correction to one keyframe in an existing orbit, not a new photograph or angle.
Target view: 01-front-driver-quarter.png
Critical grille match: The photographed grille has only TWO main rows of BIG angular clipped-rectangle openings, roughly 8 to 10 across each row with thick molded tabs, not a fine mesh. Image 3 is an approved same-truck straight-front rendering to preserve grille consistency, copy its large-aperture grille and pronounced polygonal rim around TOYOTA, adapting to target perspective. Keep target beach angle and all other truck details unchanged.
